# Small affine site induced by a morphism property

Let `P` be a morphism property of schemes and `S` be a scheme. In this file we study the small
affine `P`-site of `S`: its objects are rings `R` with a structure morphism `Spec R ⟶ S` that
satisfies `P`.

We don't make a separate definition for this site, but use
`CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.CostructuredArrow P ⊤ Scheme.Spec S`.

Under suitable assumptions on `P`, the lemmas here can be used to show that the small affine
`P`-site has the same category of sheaves as the general small `P`-site. If `P` implies
finitely generated, the small affine `P`-site is essentially small, so in particular

see the file `Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Sites.AffineEtale`.

universe u

open CategoryTheory Opposite Limits MorphismProperty

namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme

variable {S : Scheme.{u}}

/-- Construct an object of affine `P`-schemes over `S` by giving a morphism `Spec R ⟶ S`. -/
@[simps! hom left]
noncomputable def affineOverMk {P : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}} {R : CommRingCat.{u}}
    (f : Spec R ⟶ S) (hf : P f) :
    P.CostructuredArrow ⊤ Scheme.Spec S :=

end map_map

/-! ## Restriction along an explicit algebra map

The presheaf-on-algebras face of the functoriality: for consumers indexing tests by
`k`-algebra maps (limits over affine opens, the relative-Picard comparison), the base
extension is recovered from the map by `RingHom.toAlgebra`.  The instance-parameterized
`PicEtAff.map` remains the preferred form whenever a scalar tower is already in scope. -/

section mapAlg

variable {A' : Type u} [CommRing A'] [Algebra k A']

/-- Restriction of étale-plus Picard classes along an explicit `k`-algebra map of affine
tests. -/
def mapAlg (φ : A →ₐ[k] A') : PicEtAff C A →* PicEtAff C A' :=
  letI : Algebra A A' := φ.toRingHom.toAlgebra
  haveI : IsScalarTower k A A' :=
    .of_algebraMap_eq fun a => (φ.commutes a).symm
  map C A'

/-- `mapAlg` along the identity is the identity. -/
theorem mapAlg_id (a : PicEtAff C A) : mapAlg C (AlgHom.id k A) a = a :=
  map_id C a

/-- The unit of the plus construction is natural in the test algebra, explicit-map form. -/
theorem mapAlg_unit (φ : A →ₐ[k] A') (x : relPic C (overSpec k A)) :
    mapAlg C φ (unit C A x) = unit C A' (relPicAlgMap C φ x) := by
  letI : Algebra A A' := φ.toRingHom.toAlgebra
  haveI : IsScalarTower k A A' :=
    .of_algebraMap_eq fun a => (φ.commutes a).symm
  have hφ : IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k A A' = φ := AlgHom.ext fun _ => rfl
  rw [mapAlg, map_unit, hφ]

variable {A'' : Type u} [CommRing A''] [Algebra k A'']

/-- `mapAlg` along a composite is the composite of the restrictions. -/
theorem mapAlg_comp (φ : A →ₐ[k] A') (ψ : A' →ₐ[k] A'') (a : PicEtAff C A) :
    mapAlg C (ψ.comp φ) a = mapAlg C ψ (mapAlg C φ a) :=
  letI : Algebra A A' := φ.toRingHom.toAlgebra
  haveI : IsScalarTower k A A' :=
    .of_algebraMap_eq fun x => (φ.commutes x).symm
  letI : Algebra A' A'' := ψ.toRingHom.toAlgebra
  haveI : IsScalarTower k A' A'' :=
    .of_algebraMap_eq fun x => (ψ.commutes x).symm
  letI : Algebra A A'' := (ψ.comp φ).toRingHom.toAlgebra
  haveI : IsScalarTower k A A'' :=
    .of_algebraMap_eq fun x => ((ψ.comp φ).commutes x).symm
  haveI : IsScalarTower A A' A'' := .of_algebraMap_eq fun _ => rfl
  map_map C A' A'' a

end mapAlg

end PicEtAff

1266	\section{The several Picard functors}\label{sc:Pfctrs}
1267	\renewcommand{\theequation}{\thethm.\arabic{equation}}
1268	Our first job is to identify a likely candidate for the functor of
1269	points of the Picard scheme.  In fact, there are several reasonable such
1270	Picard functors, and each one is more likely to be representable than
1271	the preceding.  In this section, they all are formally introduced and
1272	compared.
1273	
1274	\begin{dfn}\label{df:aPf}
1275	 The {\it absolute Picard functor} $\Pic_X$ is the functor from  the
1276	 category of (locally Noetherian) $S$-schemes $T$ to the category of
1277	abelian groups defined by the formula
1278		$$\Pic_X(T):=\Pic(X_T).$$
1279	\end{dfn}
1280	
1281	The absolute Picard functor  is a ``prepared presheaf'' in this
1282	sense: given any family of  $S$-schemes $T_i$, we have
1283		$$\Pic_X\bigl(\textstyle\coprod T_i\bigr)=\prod\Pic_X(T_i).$$
1284	 Hence, given a covering family $\{T_i\to T\}$ in the Zariski topology,
1285	the \'etale topology, or any other Grothendieck topology on the category
1286	of $S$-schemes, there is no harm, when we consider the sheaf associated
1287	to $\Pic_X$, in working simply with the single map $T'\to T$ where
1288	$T':=\coprod T_i$.  And doing so lightens the notation, making for
1289	easier reading. Therefore, we do so throughout, calling $T'\to T$ simply
1290	a {\it covering\/} in the given topology.
1291	
1292	The absolute Picard functor $\Pic_X$ is never a separated presheaf in
1293	the Zariski topology.  Indeed, take an $S$-scheme $T$ that carries an
1294	invertible sheaf $\mc N$ such that $f^*_T\mc N$ is nontrivial.  (For
1295	example, take $T:=\I P^1_X$ and $\mc N:=\mc O_{\!T}(1)$.  Then the diagonal
1296	map $X\to X\x X$ induces a section $g$ of $f_T$; that is, $gf_T=1_T$.
1297	Hence $f^*_T\mc N$ is nontrivial.)  Now, there exists a Zariski covering
1298	$T'\to T$ such that the pullback $\mc N|T'$ is trivial; here, $T'$ is
1299	simply the disjoint union of the subsets in a suitable ordinary open
1300	covering of $T$.  So the pullback $f^*_{T'}\mc N|X_{T'}$ is trivial too.
1301	Thus $\Pic_X(T)$ has a nonzero element whose restriction is zero in

1304	According to descent theory, every representable functor is a sheaf in

1307	representable.  So, in the hope of obtaining a representable functor

4	This chapter isolates a general finiteness lemma about pairs of lattices in a module over
5	the ring of Laurent polynomials. Write \(k[T, T^{-1}]\) for the ring of Laurent polynomials
6	over a commutative ring \(k\) (Chapter~\ref{chap:Curves}): the free \(k\)-module on the
7	monomials \(T^n\), \(n \in \Z\), with multiplication \(T^m \cdot T^n = T^{m+n}\), so that
8	\(T^0 = 1\) and \(T^{-1}\) is a two-sided inverse of \(T\). For a subset \(s\) of a
9	\(k[T,T^{-1}]\)-module \(N\), write \(\langle s \rangle_{k[T,T^{-1}]}\) for the
10	\(k[T,T^{-1}]\)-submodule it generates. Call a \(k\)-module \emph{finite} if it is finitely
11	generated over \(k\), and for \(k\)-submodules \(Q_0, Q_1\) of a \(k\)-module, write
12	\(Q_0 + Q_1\) for the smallest \(k\)-submodule containing both.
13	
14	The result abstracts the classical computation, for the projective line covered by its two
15	standard affine charts, of the cohomology of a coherent sheaf as the cokernel of the
16	difference-of-restrictions map out of the two chart section rings into the ring of sections
17	on the overlap: two \(k\)-submodules \(Q_0, Q_1\) of a \(k[T,T^{-1}]\)-module \(N\), one
18	stable under multiplication by \(T\) and containing enough of \(N\), the other stable under
19	multiplication by \(T^{-1}\) and eventually absorbing every element of \(N\), leave a quotient
20	\(N / (Q_0 + Q_1)\) that is a finite \(k\)-module — because only a finite window of monomials
21	can fail to be absorbed by one lattice or the other.
22	
23	\section{Stability under powers of the generator}
24	
25	Throughout this section \(N\) is an abelian group carrying both a \(k\)-module structure and a
26	\(k[T,T^{-1}]\)-module structure (the two need not be related).
27	
28	\begin{lemma}[Stability under nonnegative powers of \(T\)]
29	  \label{lem:T_pow_stable}
30	  \lean{LaurentPolynomial.T_natCast_smul_mem}
31	  \leanok
32	  Let \(Q \subseteq N\) be a \(k\)-submodule such that \(T \cdot x \in Q\) for every
33	  \(x \in Q\). Then for every \(x \in Q\) and every integer \(m \ge 0\), \(T^m \cdot x \in Q\).
34	\end{lemma}
35	\begin{proof}
36	  \leanok
37	  Induction on \(m\). For \(m = 0\), \(T^0 \cdot x = x \in Q\). For the step, suppose
38	  \(T^m \cdot x \in Q\); then
39	  \[
40	    T^{m+1} \cdot x = T \cdot (T^m \cdot x) \in Q
41	  \]
42	  by the hypothesis on \(Q\) applied to the element \(T^m \cdot x \in Q\).
43	\end{proof}
44	
45	\begin{lemma}[Stability under nonnegative powers of \(T^{-1}\)]
46	  \label{lem:T_inv_pow_stable}
47	  \lean{LaurentPolynomial.T_neg_natCast_smul_mem}
48	  \leanok
49	  Let \(Q \subseteq N\) be a \(k\)-submodule such that \(T^{-1} \cdot x \in Q\) for every
50	  \(x \in Q\). Then for every \(x \in Q\) and every integer \(m \ge 0\),
51	  \(T^{-m} \cdot x \in Q\).
52	\end{lemma}
53	\begin{proof}
54	  \leanok
55	  Induction on \(m\), exactly as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:T_pow_stable}, with \(T^{-1}\)
56	  in place of \(T\): for \(m = 0\), \(T^0 \cdot x = x \in Q\); for the step, if
57	  \(T^{-m} \cdot x \in Q\) then
58	  \[
59	    T^{-(m+1)} \cdot x = T^{-1} \cdot (T^{-m} \cdot x) \in Q
60	  \]
61	  by the hypothesis on \(Q\).
62	\end{proof}
63	
64	\section{The two-lattice lemma}
65	
66	\begin{theorem}[Two-lattice finiteness, spanning-set form]
67	  \label{thm:two_lattice_span}
68	  \lean{LaurentPolynomial.moduleFinite_quotient_sup_of_span_eq_top}
69	  \leanok
70	  \source{hartshorne-algebraic-geometry:page-0242, hartshorne-algebraic-geometry:page-0243}
71	  Let \(k\) be a commutative ring and \(N\) a module over \(k[T,T^{-1}]\) whose
72	  \(k\)-module structure is the restriction of scalars of the \(k[T,T^{-1}]\)-action along the
73	  canonical ring map \(k \to k[T,T^{-1}]\). Let \(Q_0, Q_1 \subseteq N\) be \(k\)-submodules
74	  and \(s \subset N\) a finite subset such that:
75	  \begin{enumerate}
76	    \item \(s \subseteq Q_0\);
77	    \item \(s\) spans \(N\) over \(k[T,T^{-1}]\): \(\langle s \rangle_{k[T,T^{-1}]} = N\);
78	    \item \(Q_0\) is stable under multiplication by \(T\): \(T \cdot x \in Q_0\) for all
79	      \(x \in Q_0\);
80	    \item \(Q_1\) is stable under multiplication by \(T^{-1}\): \(T^{-1} \cdot x \in Q_1\) for
81	      all \(x \in Q_1\);
82	    \item every \(n \in N\) is eventually absorbed by \(Q_1\): there is an integer \(m \ge 0\)
83	      with \(T^{-m} \cdot n \in Q_1\).
84	  \end{enumerate}
85	  Then \(N / (Q_0 + Q_1)\) is a finite \(k\)-module: it is spanned by the classes of the
86	  monomials \(T^j \cdot x\), for \(x \in s\) and \(-M < j < 0\), where \(M\) is any uniform
87	  bound with \(T^{-M} \cdot x \in Q_1\) for every \(x \in s\).
88	\end{theorem}
89	\begin{proof}
90	  \leanok
91	  \uses{lem:T_pow_stable, lem:T_inv_pow_stable}
92	  Since \(s\) is finite, hypothesis (5) applied to each \(x \in s\) gives an integer
93	  \(m_x \ge 0\) with \(T^{-m_x} \cdot x \in Q_1\); let \(M = \max_{x \in s} m_x\) (or \(M = 0\)
94	  if \(s\) is empty). For each \(x \in s\), since \(M - m_x \ge 0\) and \(Q_1\) is stable
95	  under \(T^{-1}\), Lemma~\ref{lem:T_inv_pow_stable} gives
96	  \[
97	    T^{-M} \cdot x = T^{-(M - m_x)} \cdot \bigl(T^{-m_x} \cdot x\bigr) \in Q_1 ,
98	  \]
99	  so \(M\) is a uniform bound for all of \(s\).
100	
101	  Let \(F = \{\, T^j \cdot x : x \in s,\ -M < j < 0 \,\}\), a finite subset of \(N\) (finite
102	  since \(s\) is finite and \(j\) ranges over the \(M - 1\) integers strictly between \(-M\)
103	  and \(0\)).
104	
105	  \emph{Claim.} For every \(x \in s\) and every \(j \in \Z\),
106	  \(T^j \cdot x \in Q_0 + Q_1 + \langle F \rangle_k\), where \(\langle F \rangle_k\) is the
107	  \(k\)-submodule generated by \(F\).
108	
109	  Indeed, if \(j \ge 0\), then since \(x \in s \subseteq Q_0\) and \(Q_0\) is stable under
110	  \(T\), Lemma~\ref{lem:T_pow_stable} gives \(T^j \cdot x \in Q_0\). If \(j \le -M\), write
111	  \(j = -d - M\) with \(d = -j - M \ge 0\); then
112	  \[
113	    T^j \cdot x = T^{-d} \cdot \bigl(T^{-M} \cdot x\bigr) ,
114	  \]
115	  and since \(T^{-M} \cdot x \in Q_1\) and \(Q_1\) is stable under \(T^{-1}\),
116	  Lemma~\ref{lem:T_inv_pow_stable} gives \(T^j \cdot x \in Q_1\). Finally, if \(-M < j < 0\),
117	  then \(T^j \cdot x \in F \subseteq \langle F \rangle_k\) by definition of \(F\). This proves
118	  the claim.
119	
120	  Every element \(f \in k[T,T^{-1}]\) is, by definition of the Laurent polynomial ring, a
121	  \(k\)-linear combination of finitely many monomials \(T^j\), \(j \in \Z\). Since
122	  \(Q_0 + Q_1 + \langle F \rangle_k\) is a \(k\)-submodule of \(N\), the claim and this
123	  decomposition of \(f\) give, for every \(x \in s\),
124	  \[
125	    f \cdot x \in Q_0 + Q_1 + \langle F \rangle_k .
126	  \]
127	  Now let \(n \in N\) be arbitrary. By hypothesis (2), \(n\) is a (finite) \(k[T,T^{-1}]\)-
128	  linear combination \(n = \sum_{x \in s} f_x \cdot x\) of elements of \(s\); each summand lies
129	  in \(Q_0 + Q_1 + \langle F \rangle_k\) by the previous paragraph, and this submodule is
130	  closed under addition, so \(n \in Q_0 + Q_1 + \langle F \rangle_k\). Hence
131	  \[
132	    Q_0 + Q_1 + \langle F \rangle_k = N .
133	  \]
134	  Consequently the composite \(\langle F \rangle_k \hookrightarrow N \twoheadrightarrow
135	  N/(Q_0+Q_1)\) is surjective, so the (finite) image of \(F\) in \(N/(Q_0+Q_1)\) spans it as a
136	  \(k\)-module. Thus \(N/(Q_0+Q_1)\) is a finite \(k\)-module.
137	\end{proof}
138	
139	\section{Localization forms}
140	
141	The spanning-set form of Theorem~\ref{thm:two_lattice_span} is inconvenient when only a
142	localization-type hypothesis on \(Q_0\) is available, symmetric to hypothesis (5) on \(Q_1\):
143	every element of \(N\) is eventually absorbed by \(Q_0\) after multiplying by a sufficiently
144	large power of \(T\). The next two results derive the finiteness conclusion from this
145	symmetric pair of hypotheses, at the cost of assuming \(N\) itself is a finite
146	\(k[T,T^{-1}]\)-module; this is exactly the shape of hypothesis produced by localizing a
147	finite module away from an element.
148	
149	\begin{corollary}[Two-lattice finiteness, localization form]
150	  \label{cor:two_lattice_loc}
151	  \lean{LaurentPolynomial.moduleFinite_quotient_sup_of_exists_smul_mem}
152	  \leanok
153	  Let \(k\) be a commutative ring and \(N\) a finite module over \(k[T,T^{-1}]\) whose
154	  \(k\)-module structure is the restriction of scalars of the \(k[T,T^{-1}]\)-action along the
155	  canonical ring map \(k \to k[T,T^{-1}]\). Let \(Q_0, Q_1 \subseteq N\) be \(k\)-submodules
156	  such that:
157	  \begin{enumerate}
158	    \item \(Q_0\) is stable under multiplication by \(T\);
159	    \item \(Q_1\) is stable under multiplication by \(T^{-1}\);
160	    \item every \(n \in N\) is eventually absorbed by \(Q_0\): there is an integer \(m \ge 0\)
161	      with \(T^m \cdot n \in Q_0\);
162	    \item every \(n \in N\) is eventually absorbed by \(Q_1\): there is an integer \(m \ge 0\)
163	      with \(T^{-m} \cdot n \in Q_1\).
164	  \end{enumerate}
165	  Then \(N / (Q_0 + Q_1)\) is a finite \(k\)-module.
166	\end{corollary}
167	\begin{proof}
168	  \leanok
169	  \uses{thm:two_lattice_span}
170	  Since \(N\) is a finite \(k[T,T^{-1}]\)-module, choose a finite subset \(t \subset N\) with
171	  \(\langle t \rangle_{k[T,T^{-1}]} = N\). By hypothesis (3), for each \(y \in t\) choose an
172	  integer \(\mu(y) \ge 0\) with \(T^{\mu(y)} \cdot y \in Q_0\), and set
173	  \[
174	    s = \{\, T^{\mu(y)} \cdot y : y \in t \,\} \subseteq Q_0 ,
175	  \]
176	  a finite subset of \(N\).
177	
178	  The set \(s\) again spans \(N\) over \(k[T,T^{-1}]\): each element of \(s\) is a
179	  \(k[T,T^{-1}]\)-multiple of an element of \(t\), so
180	  \(\langle s \rangle_{k[T,T^{-1}]} \subseteq \langle t \rangle_{k[T,T^{-1}]} = N\); and since
181	  \(T\) is invertible in \(k[T,T^{-1}]\) with inverse \(T^{-1}\), every \(y \in t\) is
182	  recovered from \(s\) by
183	  \[
184	    y = T^{-\mu(y)} \cdot \bigl(T^{\mu(y)} \cdot y\bigr) ,
185	  \]
186	  a \(k[T,T^{-1}]\)-multiple of the element \(T^{\mu(y)} \cdot y \in s\); so
187	  \(t \subseteq \langle s \rangle_{k[T,T^{-1}]}\), giving
188	  \(\langle s \rangle_{k[T,T^{-1}]} \supseteq \langle t \rangle_{k[T,T^{-1}]} = N\) as well.
189	  Hence \(\langle s \rangle_{k[T,T^{-1}]} = N\).
190	
191	  Now \(s \subseteq Q_0\), \(s\) spans \(N\) over \(k[T,T^{-1}]\), \(Q_0\) is \(T\)-stable,
192	  \(Q_1\) is \(T^{-1}\)-stable, and hypothesis (4) is exactly hypothesis (5) of
193	  Theorem~\ref{thm:two_lattice_span}. Applying that theorem to \(s\), \(Q_0\), \(Q_1\) gives
194	  that \(N/(Q_0+Q_1)\) is a finite \(k\)-module.
195	\end{proof}
196	
197	\begin{corollary}[Two-lattice finiteness, localization form via powers of the generator]
198	  \label{cor:two_lattice_loc_pow}
199	  \lean{LaurentPolynomial.moduleFinite_quotient_sup_of_exists_pow_smul_mem}
200	  \leanok
201	  Let \(k\), \(N\), \(Q_0\), \(Q_1\) be as in Corollary~\ref{cor:two_lattice_loc}, satisfying
202	  hypotheses (1) and (2) there, and suppose in place of (3) and (4) that:
203	  \begin{enumerate}
204	    \item[(3a)] every \(n \in N\) satisfies: there is an integer \(m \ge 0\) with
205	      \(T^m \cdot n \in Q_0\), where \(T^m\) denotes the ordinary \(m\)-th power of the ring
206	      element \(T \in k[T,T^{-1}]\);
207	    \item[(4a)] every \(n \in N\) satisfies: there is an integer \(m \ge 0\) with
208	      \(T^{-m} \cdot n \in Q_1\), where \(T^{-m}\) denotes the ordinary \(m\)-th power of
209	      \(T^{-1} \in k[T,T^{-1}]\).
210	  \end{enumerate}
211	  Then \(N / (Q_0 + Q_1)\) is a finite \(k\)-module.
212	\end{corollary}
213	\begin{proof}
214	  \leanok
215	  \uses{cor:two_lattice_loc}
216	  For every integer \(m \ge 0\), the \(m\)-th power of the ring element \(T\) is the monomial
217	  \(T^m\), and the \(m\)-th power of \(T^{-1}\) is the monomial \(T^{-m}\); so hypotheses
218	  (3a) and (4a) here coincide, element for element, with hypotheses (3) and (4) of
219	  Corollary~\ref{cor:two_lattice_loc}. The conclusion is immediate from that corollary.
220	\end{proof}

5	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.UnitsCocycle
6	
7	/-!
8	# The definitional Picard group: Čech `H¹` of the units presheaf
9	
10	For a scheme `X`, this file defines the Picard group of record of this development:
11	the Čech cohomology `Ȟ¹(X, 𝒪_X^*)` on the small Zariski site, computed on **pointed
12	covers** (one open per point of `X`, `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.UnitsCocycle`) and
13	stabilized along the refinement preorder.
14	
15	## Main declarations
16	
17	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CechPic`: the Picard group `Ȟ¹(X, 𝒪_X^*)` as the quotient
18	  of `Σ 𝒰, X.unitsH1 𝒰` by agreement on a common refinement, with its `CommGroup`
19	  structure and the constructor/eliminator API `CechPic.mk`, `CechPic.ind`,
20	  `CechPic.mk_eq_mk_iff`, `CechPic.mk_unitsRes`, `CechPic.mk_mul_mk_inf`.
21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CechPic.map`: contravariant functoriality — for
22	  `f : X ⟶ Y` the pullback `Y.CechPic →* X.CechPic` — with the strict functor laws
23	  `CechPic.map_id` and `CechPic.map_comp` (the lane keystone).
24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CechPic.subsingleton_of_subsingleton`: on a scheme with a
25	  subsingleton underlying space (e.g. `Spec` of a field) the Picard group is trivial.
26	-/
27	
28	set_option autoImplicit false
29	
30	universe u
31	
32	open CategoryTheory Opposite CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups
33	
34	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
35	
36	namespace Scheme
37	
38	variable {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}}
39	
40	/-! ## The Picard group  -/
41	
42	instance cechPicSetoid (X : Scheme.{u}) : Setoid (Σ 𝒰 : X.PointedCover, X.unitsH1 𝒰) where
43	  r p q := ∃ (𝒲 : X.PointedCover) (h₁ : 𝒲 ≤ p.1) (h₂ : 𝒲 ≤ q.1),
44	    unitsRes h₁ p.2 = unitsRes h₂ q.2
45	  iseqv := by
46	    constructor
47	    · exact fun p ↦ ⟨p.1, le_rfl, le_rfl, rfl⟩
48	    · rintro p q ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, e⟩
49	      exact ⟨𝒲, h₂, h₁, e.symm⟩
50	    · rintro p q r ⟨𝒲₁, h₁, h₂, e₁⟩ ⟨𝒲₂, h₃, h₄, e₂⟩
51	      refine ⟨𝒲₁ ⊓ 𝒲₂, inf_le_left.trans h₁, inf_le_right.trans h₄, ?_⟩
52	      have e₁' := congrArg (unitsRes (inf_le_left : 𝒲₁ ⊓ 𝒲₂ ≤ 𝒲₁)) e₁
53	      have e₂' := congrArg (unitsRes (inf_le_right : 𝒲₁ ⊓ 𝒲₂ ≤ 𝒲₂)) e₂
54	      simp only [unitsRes_unitsRes] at e₁' e₂'
55	      exact e₁'.trans e₂'
56	
57	/-- The definitional Picard group of a scheme: Čech `H¹` of the units presheaf,
58	stabilized along refinement of pointed covers. -/
59	def CechPic (X : Scheme.{u}) : Type u :=
60	  Quotient (cechPicSetoid X)
61	
62	namespace CechPic
63	
64	/-- The Picard class of a unit Čech `H¹` class on a pointed cover. -/
65	def mk (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) (a : X.unitsH1 𝒰) : X.CechPic :=
66	  ⟦⟨𝒰, a⟩⟧
67	
68	@[elab_as_elim]
69	theorem ind {motive : X.CechPic → Prop}
70	    (mk : ∀ (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) (a : X.unitsH1 𝒰), motive (mk 𝒰 a)) (x : X.CechPic) :
71	    motive x :=
72	  Quotient.ind (fun p ↦ by obtain ⟨𝒰, a⟩ := p; exact mk 𝒰 a) x
73	
74	theorem mk_eq_mk_iff {𝒰 𝒱 : X.PointedCover} {a : X.unitsH1 𝒰} {b : X.unitsH1 𝒱} :
75	    mk 𝒰 a = mk 𝒱 b ↔
76	      ∃ (𝒲 : X.PointedCover) (h₁ : 𝒲 ≤ 𝒰) (h₂ : 𝒲 ≤ 𝒱),
77	        unitsRes h₁ a = unitsRes h₂ b :=
78	  Quotient.eq
79	
80	/-- Two classes agreeing after restriction to a common refinement are equal; in
81	particular `mk` is invariant under restriction. -/
82	@[simp]
83	theorem mk_unitsRes {𝒰 𝒱 : X.PointedCover} (h : 𝒱 ≤ 𝒰) (a : X.unitsH1 𝒰) :
84	    mk 𝒱 (unitsRes h a) = mk 𝒰 a :=
85	  Quotient.sound ⟨𝒱, le_rfl, h, unitsRes_rfl _⟩
86	
87	private def mulSig (p q : Σ 𝒰 : X.PointedCover, X.unitsH1 𝒰) :
88	    Σ 𝒰 : X.PointedCover, X.unitsH1 𝒰 :=
89	  ⟨p.1 ⊓ q.1, unitsRes inf_le_left p.2 * unitsRes inf_le_right q.2⟩
90	
91	private lemma mulSig_assoc {𝒰 𝒱 𝒳 : X.PointedCover} (a : X.unitsH1 𝒰) (b : X.unitsH1 𝒱)
92	    (c : X.unitsH1 𝒳) :
93	    mk (𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱 ⊓ 𝒳)
94	        (unitsRes inf_le_left (unitsRes inf_le_left a * unitsRes inf_le_right b) *
95	          unitsRes inf_le_right c)
96	      = mk (𝒰 ⊓ (𝒱 ⊓ 𝒳))
97	        (unitsRes inf_le_left a *
98	          unitsRes inf_le_right (unitsRes inf_le_left b * unitsRes inf_le_right c)) := by
99	  refine mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr ⟨𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱 ⊓ 𝒳, le_rfl, (inf_assoc 𝒰 𝒱 𝒳).le, ?_⟩
100	  simp only [map_mul, unitsRes_unitsRes, unitsRes_rfl]
101	  exact mul_assoc _ _ _
102	
103	private lemma mulSig_compat {p p' q q' : Σ 𝒰 : X.PointedCover, X.unitsH1 𝒰}
104	    (hp : p ≈ p') (hq : q ≈ q') : mulSig p q ≈ mulSig p' q' := by
105	  obtain ⟨𝒲₁, h₁, h₂, e₁⟩ := hp
106	  obtain ⟨𝒲₂, h₃, h₄, e₂⟩ := hq
107	  have e₁' := congrArg (unitsRes (inf_le_left : 𝒲₁ ⊓ 𝒲₂ ≤ 𝒲₁)) e₁
108	  have e₂' := congrArg (unitsRes (inf_le_right : 𝒲₁ ⊓ 𝒲₂ ≤ 𝒲₂)) e₂
109	  simp only [unitsRes_unitsRes] at e₁' e₂'
110	  refine ⟨𝒲₁ ⊓ 𝒲₂, inf_le_inf h₁ h₃, inf_le_inf h₂ h₄, ?_⟩
111	  show unitsRes (inf_le_inf h₁ h₃) (unitsRes inf_le_left p.2 * unitsRes inf_le_right q.2)
112	      = unitsRes (inf_le_inf h₂ h₄) (unitsRes inf_le_left p'.2 * unitsRes inf_le_right q'.2)
113	  simp only [map_mul, unitsRes_unitsRes]
114	  rw [e₁', e₂']
115	
116	instance : CommGroup X.CechPic where
117	  mul := Quotient.map₂ mulSig (fun _ _ hp _ _ hq ↦ mulSig_compat hp hq)
118	  one := mk ⊤ 1
119	  inv := Quotient.map (fun p ↦ ⟨p.1, p.2⁻¹⟩) (by

122	  mul_assoc a b c := by

124	    induction b using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒱 b =>

129	    show mk (⊤ ⊓ 𝒰) (unitsRes inf_le_left (1 : X.unitsH1 ⊤) * unitsRes inf_le_right a)
130	      = mk 𝒰 a
131	    rw [map_one, one_mul, mk_unitsRes]

133	    induction a using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒰 a =>
134	    show mk (𝒰 ⊓ ⊤) (unitsRes inf_le_left a * unitsRes inf_le_right (1 : X.unitsH1 ⊤))

187	    ∀ {p q : Σ 𝒰 : Y.PointedCover, Y.unitsH1 𝒰}, p ≈ q → mapSig f p ≈ mapSig f q := by

237	  refine MonoidHom.ext fun x ↦ ?_
238	  induction x using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒰 a =>
239	  show mk (𝒰.pullback (f ≫ g)) ((f ≫ g).pullbackUnitsH1 𝒰 a)
240	    = mk ((𝒰.pullback g).pullback f)
241	        (f.pullbackUnitsH1 (𝒰.pullback g) (g.pullbackUnitsH1 𝒰 a))
242	  have hle : 𝒰.pullback (f ≫ g) ≤ (𝒰.pullback g).pullback f := fun x ↦ le_of_eq (by simp)
243	  refine mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr ⟨𝒰.pullback (f ≫ g), le_rfl, hle, ?_⟩
244	  induction a using Quot.ind with | _ γ =>
245	  refine congrArg (Quot.mk _) ?_
246	  ext x y T a b

248	    Hom.pullbackUnitsCocycle_ev, Hom.pullbackUnitsCocycle_unitsEvInf, unitsAppLE_unitsAppLE]

255	every unit cocycle is a coboundary. -/

269	  Subsingleton.elim x 1

/-!
# Cohomology of an object of the site with `ModuleCat k` coefficients

For a sheaf of `R`-modules `F` on a small site `(C, J)` and an object `U : C`, this file
defines the cohomology `Sheaf.HModule' F U n` of `U` with coefficients in `F`: the
`Ext`-group from the *free sheaf of `R`-modules on `U`* (the sheafification of the
composite `yoneda.obj U ⋙ ModuleCat.free R`) to `F`. This mirrors mathlib's
`CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H'` (which is `AddCommGrpCat`-valued) at `ModuleCat R`, so that the
Mayer–Vietoris (0,1)-slice can be run `R`-linearly
(`AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.MayerVietoris`).

## Main definitions

* `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.freeModuleSheaf J R U` — the free sheaf of `R`-modules on `U`.
* `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.freeModuleSheafMap J R i` — functoriality in `U`.
* `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.freeModuleSheafHomEquiv` — the `R`-linear "universal property of
  sections": `(freeModuleSheaf J R U ⟶ F) ≃ₗ[R] F(U)`, with naturality in `F`
  (`freeModuleSheafHomEquiv_comp`) and in `U` (`freeModuleSheafHomEquiv_map`).
* `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.HModule' F U n` — `Ext^n(R[U], F)`, a `Type u` with a `Module R`
  structure.
* `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.HModule'.linearEquiv₀` — `H'⁰(U, F) ≃ₗ[R] F(U)`.
* `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.freeModuleSheafIsoConstModuleSheaf` — for a terminal object `T`,
  the canonical isomorphism `R[T] ≅ R_X` with the constant sheaf, whence
  `Sheaf.HModule.linearEquivHModule' : HModule F n ≃ₗ[R] HModule' F T n`: cohomology of
  the site (`Sheaf.HModule`) is cohomology of a terminal object.

## Implementation notes

Morphisms out of `freeModuleSheaf J R U` are computed from the sheafification universal
property (`sheafifyLift`) against the explicit presheaf morphism `freeModuleSheafDesc`
determined by a section `s ∈ F(U)`; no adjunction unfolding is needed. All elementwise
computations are routed through `ModuleCat.free_hom_ext` after a `change` to the
`ModuleCat.Hom.hom` spelling (the concrete-category coercion produced by `free_hom_ext`
is only defeq to it, and `rw` chokes on the mismatch otherwise). The whole file is
single-universe (`Type u` site, `ModuleCat.{u} R` coefficients), matching
`AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.ModuleKSheaf`.
-/

open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite

namespace ModuleCat

/-- The free module functor preserves monomorphisms (mapping along an injection of index
types is injective on finitely supported functions). Mirrors the mathlib instance for
`AddCommGrpCat.free`. -/
instance free_preservesMonomorphisms (R : Type u) [Ring R] :
    (ModuleCat.free R).PreservesMonomorphisms where
  preserves {X Y} f hf := by
    rw [ModuleCat.mono_iff_injective]
    exact Finsupp.mapDomain_injective ((CategoryTheory.mono_iff_injective f).mp hf)

# AlgebraicJacobian (rebuild)

<!-- archon:readme -->

## Project

A **from-scratch rebuild** of the Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization of the **Jacobian of a smooth,
proper, geometrically irreducible curve** over a field (Christian Merten's AI challenge, inspired by
Kevin Buzzard's Riemann-surface version). By a smooth curve we mean a geometrically irreducible,
smooth scheme of relative dimension one over a field.

This project supplies the missing definitions (`genus`, `Jacobian`, the Abel–Jacobi map `ofCurve`)
and theorems (the Jacobian is smooth of relative dimension equal to the genus, proper, geometrically
irreducible, and is the Albanese variety of the curve, characterized by the universal property
`exists_unique_ofCurve_comp`). It targets the **extended** challenge: additionally, the Jacobian is
**functorial** in the curve (`Jacobian.functor`) and **commutes with base change of fields**
(`baseChangeIso` with identity and cocycle coherences, and Abel–Jacobi compatibility
`baseChange_ofCurve`), which makes the construction canonical.

It is rebuilt rather than continued: the goal is a cleaner, more general, mathlib-idiomatic
infrastructure and a shorter, clearer path to the conclusion. The existing project
`MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge` may be **read** when genuinely blocked, but nothing is
copied from it — every declaration is rewritten. The rebuild is driven by its Archon Horizon task,
which carries the full charter (target, constraints, working model, and phases).
